title: OpenAI · Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra
date: Published 11 September 2026
summary: Reassess accumulated instructions when moving to Astra; elaborate procedures can constrain a stronger model.
Keep skill triggers precise and load supporting material only when relevant.
Replace blanket document-reading and repeated-testing demands with context-sensitive guidance.
application: Audit existing instructions before adding another skill.
limits: Practical guidance from Eric Provencher, not a controlled measurement of skill gains on Astra.

title: OpenAI · Building games with Astra
date: Published 4 September 2026
summary: Begin with the desired player experience and visual references.
The example uses TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js with inspectable game state.
Separate repeatable scene setup from tests that actually operate the controls.
application: Ground the game brief and verification plan in a current Astra example.
limits: Thomas Ricouard’s showcase is an implementation account; it does not establish typical success rates.

title: SkillAlchemy · Open-World Agent Skill Creation
date: Submitted 24 August 2026 · v1 reviewed
summary: Discovers task requirements and supporting external evidence before compiling a reusable skill.
Reports improvements over no-skill and automated-generation baselines on 87 SkillsBench v1.1 tasks.
Evaluations include GPT-5.5, Opus 4.8, and DeepSeek V4 configurations; none is Astra.
application: Treat evidence-led skill generation as a candidate worth testing.
limits: Preprint results do not show that casually generating a skill for any task will help.

title: SkillsBench · Agent leaderboard, v1.1
date: Leaderboard recomputed 16 July 2026 · underlying project began before March
summary: Compares skills and no-skills conditions across a broad collection of 87 tasks.
The reviewed table contains 24 paired agent–model configurations plus one with-skills-only result.
Curated skills often help, but the size of the benefit varies across configurations.
application: Useful counterevidence to the claim that all skills are redundant.
limits: The reviewed leaderboard has no Astra entry. Different harnesses and task mixes limit transfer to game development.

title: SkillsInjector · Dynamic Skill Context Construction for LLM Agents
date: Submitted 28 May 2026 · v1 reviewed
summary: Selects skills for the current task and adapts how much skill context to include.
Studies interactions between descriptions, context budget, and selection; adding more skills is not consistently better.
Reports improvements on three benchmarks using Qwen-based agents.
application: Evaluate which skill was selected as well as the final output.
limits: A proposed research method, not a feature claimed for Codex. The tested agents are not Astra.

title: Anthropic · Harness design for long-running application development
date: Published 24 March 2026
summary: Uses explicit quality criteria and a generator/evaluator loop for application work.
Revisits the surrounding workflow as model capabilities improve.
Simplifies intermediate scaffolding with Opus 4.6 while retaining useful planning and evaluation roles.
application: Reassess the older long-running-agent recipe instead of copying it unchanged.
limits: Claude application experiments do not determine the best number of agents or milestones for an Astra game.

title: SWE-Skills-Bench · Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?
date: Submitted 16 March 2026 · v1 reviewed
summary: Evaluates 49 public software-engineering skills on roughly 565 tasks with executable acceptance checks.
Reports no gain for 39 of 49 skills and a small average improvement of about 1.2 percentage points.
Finds overhead and some regressions, including mismatches between advice and repository versions.
application: Keep a no-added-skill baseline and examine regressions, not just aggregate wins.
limits: Explicitly preliminary; uses Claude Code with Haiku 4.5, not Astra. Its setup differs from SkillsBench and Codex skill routing.

title: OpenAI · GPT-6 Astra prompting best practices
date: Live documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Makes model-specific prompting recommendations for Astra.
Clarifies autonomy, instruction-file behavior, and boundaries for delegated work.
Recommends verification proportionate to the task.
application: Inform the agent’s working agreement; keep game mechanics as separate design decisions.
limits: A moving documentation URL may later describe another model. Confirm its heading before reusing the advice.

title: OpenAI · Build skills
date: Live documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: A skill packages SKILL.md metadata and instructions, with optional scripts, references, and assets.
Supports explicit selection and implicit matching to the task through its description.
The initial catalog is budgeted; selected skills then supply their full instructions.
application: Check available skills before authoring a duplicate. Repository skills can live in .agents/skills.
limits: Availability is required. Automatic matching is not a guarantee of correct selection or internet-wide skill discovery.

title: OpenAI · Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
date: Live documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Explains how repository instructions are discovered and scoped.
Parent instructions and more local instructions can both affect a task.
Repository guidance supplies persistent conventions across sessions.
application: Record commands and local conventions in a short, accurate instruction file.
limits: This mechanism is distinct from selecting a skill. Our downloadable example is not active in this book repository.

title: GitHub · Spec Kit
date: Live documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Organizes work around specification, planning, tasks, and implementation.
Makes requirements and technical decisions explicit before they spread through code.
Provides tooling and templates for a specification-driven workflow.
application: Borrow the separation of decisions; one page can be enough for Signal Garden.
limits: Workflow documentation is not evidence that installing the toolkit improves every small project or Astra run.

title: Godot · Your first 3D game
date: Stable documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Builds a small 3D game through a sequence of practical lessons.
Introduces scene organization, movement, enemies, collisions, and interface elements.
Shows how individual engine concepts combine into a playable result.
application: Use a focused lesson when an engine concept blocks progress.
limits: Match the documentation to the installed Godot version. A tutorial does not evaluate an AI workflow.

title: Godot · Exporting for the Web
date: Stable documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Web export uses WebGL 2 and the Compatibility renderer; Godot 4 C# web export remains unavailable in the reviewed guidance.
Threaded builds introduce hosting isolation requirements; single-thread export has different constraints.
Browser input, audio, and hosting behavior require explicit attention.
application: Try a tiny export on the intended host before building the full game.
limits: Check the exact engine release. A model upgrade does not remove browser or hosting restrictions.

title: Vite · Deploying a Static Site
date: Live documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Production builds normally generate the dist directory.
GitHub Pages project sites need a base path matching the repository name.
The guide provides a GitHub Actions deployment example.
application: Build and test the game at its eventual repository subpath.
limits: Applies to the proposed Vite game. This book uses its own dependency-free static builder.

title: GitHub · Using custom workflows with GitHub Pages
date: Live documentation · publication/update date not stated
summary: Separates the build artifact from the deployment job.
Describes Pages setup, artifact upload, deployment permissions, and the github-pages environment.
Requires the deployment job to receive the appropriate artifact and authorization.
application: Publish only the generated dist output and inspect the completed deployment.
limits: A successful workflow does not prove correct asset paths or playable browser behavior.

title: Three.js · README
date: Live repository · no single publication date used
summary: Provides a JavaScript library for displaying interactive 3D content.
Links installation guidance, documentation, examples, and rendering capabilities.
Its rendering focus leaves game rules and application structure to the developer.
application: A suitable starting library for a small browser game with custom mechanics.
limits: The README is a capability reference, not a performance comparison with other engines. Pin the installed version.

title: Babylon.js · Specifications
date: Live feature reference · publication/update date not stated
summary: Lists the browser engine’s rendering and scene capabilities.
Covers integrated tooling and physics-related support.
Provides a feature checklist for assessing an engine-oriented browser stack.
application: Consider Babylon.js when its existing systems match the game’s needs.
limits: Feature availability does not establish usability or speed on your project; this book ran no engine benchmark.

title: Unity · Web browser compatibility
date: Live manual · Unity 6.6 page reviewed; publication/update date not stated
summary: Defines supported browser requirements for Unity web content.
WebGL 2, WebAssembly, and browser/platform compatibility matter to deployment.
Compatibility must be assessed against the Unity release and target device.
application: Test an export in the actual target browser before committing to this stack.
limits: Avoid applying older blanket claims about browser support to a newer Unity version.

title: Anthropic · Effective harnesses for long-running agents
date: Published 26 November 2025
summary: Separates initial project setup from subsequent incremental feature work.
Uses progress records and Git history to help later sessions resume.
Emphasizes browser checks for end-to-end behavior.
application: Retain recoverable progress and observable completion; reassess the amount of scaffolding.
limits: Read with the March 2026 follow-up [21]. Its earlier agent setup is not an Astra prescription.

title: Andrej Karpathy · Software Is Changing (Again)
date: Talk published 17 June 2025
summary: AI generation creates a corresponding human verification workload.
Concrete requests and inspectable intermediate artifacts can make review easier.
A large generated diff still demands substantial scrutiny; search the transcript for “verification”.
application: Keep observable game checks; current Astra game guidance [04] provides a newer practical example.
limits: Selected transcript passage, not a full talk synopsis or benchmark. No stable timecodes were available; captions can contain errors.

title: Andrej Karpathy · How I use LLMs
date: Video published February 2025
summary: Explains the context window using a working-memory analogy.
Search supplies outside information to the current conversation.
Distinguishes supplied context from knowledge learned during training; locate “working memory” in the transcript.
application: Supply relevant current evidence. Astra-specific guidance [17] updates how much context to require.
limits: Selected passage only. Historical product names and account details are excluded from current setup advice.

type: Creator’s written tutorial · associated YouTube video
title: GDQuest · Your first 3D game with Godot 4
date: 2025 course · exact publication day not used
summary: The accessible written course builds a Survivor Arena FPS in Godot 4.
Uses a concrete small game to introduce 3D development concepts.
Connects lessons to a playable project that can be examined and adapted.
application: Use as a learning exercise alongside current Godot documentation [09] and export constraints [11].
limits: Video NJJNWGD25rg had no usable transcript retrieved. These notes summarize the written course, not unseen video content.
